name: 重生的世界
english_description: A Taiwan-origin (Traditional Chinese, BIG5-encoded), MudOS v22.2b14-era mudlib whose own README describes an economic-simulation MUD -- players occupy land, found cities/governments, build houses/shops/warehouses, farm and manufacture goods through an agricultural-then-industrial-then-knowledge-era production chain, and trade on an in-game stock market -- distinct from the Chinese-wuxia-combat family that dominates most of this collection's Simplified-Chinese libs; RevivalWorld is English-named in its own source (RWlib) and content (city/area/quest names are English, e.g. a 'Suphia and Benjamin' quest chain). This lib was built against a heavily custom-patched MudOS driver (its own doc/driver/modify/source_files/ ships the C source of the patches) providing several driver-level efuns that this project's stock FluffOS build does not have: an F_DBASE-style set()/query()/delete()/addn() (+_temp variants) property-storage system keyed by "/"-separated paths reflecting on a plain `database` mapping variable (restored as real methods on the DATABASE feature plus a previous_object()-redirecting simul_efun fallback for objects, like login_ob.lpc, that declare their own standalone `database` variable without inheriting that feature); an ansi package (ansi()/remove_ansi()/noansi_strlen()/kill_repeat_ansi()/ansi_part(), reimplemented run-length rather than character-by-character since a naive per-character rebuild is quadratic enough to blow a 30-second eval-cost budget on this driver's heavily ANSI-colored map-rendering HTML page); an arith_operator package for big-number decimal-string math (reimplemented with native 64-bit int arithmetic, ample for this lib's real value ranges); and a chinese package (cwrap() word-wrap ported from BIG5-byte-width detection to Unicode-codepoint width detection; B2G()/G2B()/bg5cc() raw-byte BIG5<->GBK re-encoding helpers restored as no-op passthroughs since there is no byte-level encoding left to convert once everything is UTF-8). Also fixed: creator.lpc's boot-time #define-header generator (creates include/{feature,inherit,daemon,condition}.h by scanning the source tree) had the exact same [0..<3]-strips-".c"/[<2..<1]-checks-".c" extension-width bugs as the mechanical .c->.lpc rename elsewhere, but here they silently WIPED all four generated headers back down to empty stubs on every boot (their own generator loop matched zero files) until fixed to [0..<5]/[<4..<1] -- since virtually every macro this lib's daemons/commands/simul_efuns use (including the ones simul_efun.lpc itself needs to even compile) comes from those four files, this was the single highest-impact fix in the whole port; the identical extension-width bug independently in command_d.lpc's own command-dispatch table (silently registering every player command under the wrong verb name) and in system_d.lpc's preload-list filter (silently dropping every preloaded daemon, including the ones the mudlib's own comments say must load first); a hardcoded 3-separate-port login architecture (real player port 5000 / wizard-only port 5001 / special-client port 5002, baked into login.h) that made every connection to this project's single real port dispatch nowhere and just hang with no banner; a missing get_root_uid()/get_bb_uid()/creator_file() trio on master.lpc under this driver's PACKAGE_UIDS build; and, found only via live registration testing all the way to actual world entry, an unguarded restore_object() against a save-format-incompatible shipped emote_d.lpc save file throwing (rather than failing gracefully) from deep inside command_d.lpc's own command-table rebuild, silently preventing every single player command from ever registering, site-wide, from the very first boot. Verified end-to-end via raw socket registration tests reaching real world entry and a working `look` command, and a seeded fluffos/Mud@2026 admin account confirmed live with real (admin)-equivalent status.
